paragraphs: Art. 2. (1) Municipal property is:
1. the properties and things set by law;
2. the properties and things given to the municipality in ownership by law;
3. the properties whose ownership was restored to the municipality under the conditions and procedure of a law;
4. the properties and things donated or bequeathed to the municipality;
5. the properties and things acquired by the municipality with voluntary work and/or money of the population;
6. the properties and things acquired by the municipality in the liquidation of commercial companies with municipal participation;
7. the properties and things acquired by the municipality by a legal transaction, by prescription or in another way set by law.
(2) The properties and things of commercial companies and non-profit legal entities are not municipal property, even if the municipality was the only owner of the property transferred to them.
Art. 3. (1) Municipal property is public and private.
(2) Public municipal property is:
1. the properties and things set by law;
2. the properties intended for the functions of the bodies of local self-government and local administration;
3. other properties intended for the lasting satisfaction of public needs of local importance, set by the municipal council.

(3) Private municipal property is all other municipal properties and things. The fruits and the income of properties and things that are public municipal property are private property of the municipality.
Art. 5. (1) The municipality certifies the creation, the change and the end of its right of ownership of properties with an act of municipal property.
(2) The act of municipal property is an official document made by an official in the procedure and form set by law.
(3) The act of municipal property has no constitutive effect.
Art. 6. (1) Properties and things that are public municipal property and no longer serve the purpose under Art. 3(2) are declared private municipal property by the municipal council.
(2) Properties and things that are private municipal property and have acquired the purpose under Art. 3(2) are declared public municipal property.
(3) The decisions of the municipal council under para. 1 are adopted by a majority of two thirds of all councillors, and those under para. 2 by more than half of all councillors.
Art. 7. (1) Properties and things that are public municipal property, the land of the municipal land fund and the forest territories that are municipal property cannot be acquired by prescription.

(2) Properties and things that are public municipal property cannot be alienated or transferred to third persons, except to the state under the conditions and procedure of a special law; in these cases the state cannot change the public character of the property. Properties that are public municipal property may be burdened with limited real rights only in the cases set by law.
(3) Properties and things that are private municipal property can be the object of disposal. The general rules on property apply to them, unless a law provides otherwise.
(4) The ownership of properties that are public municipal property is not subject to restitution.
Art. 34. (1) The municipality acquires ownership and limited real rights by a legal transaction, by prescription or in another way set by law.

(2) Ownership or limited real rights in properties are acquired for value after a decision of the municipal council, in the procedure of the ordinance under Art. 8(2). The mayor concludes the contract on the basis of the decision.
(3) Gifts and bequests are accepted by the mayor under the conditions of Art. 61(2) of the Inheritance Act.

(4) The municipality disposes of properties and things that are private municipal property by sale, exchange, gift, partition, creation of limited real rights for value or free of charge, or in another way set by law.
(5) (Repealed.)
(6) Limited real rights in objects that are public municipal property are created under the conditions and procedure set by law.

(7) The contracts for the acquisition of ownership and limited real rights in properties, and for the disposal of municipal properties, are concluded in written form by the mayor and are entered on the order of the registration judge of the property's location. Contracts for exchanges of municipal properties with properties of natural or legal persons are entered at the location of the municipal property, and exchanges with state properties at the location of the state property.
(8) At the date of the contracts of disposal under para. 7, the acts for the municipal properties must be entered in the registry office.

Art. 35. (1) The sale of properties and things that are private municipal property is made, after a decision of the municipal council, by the mayor by a public auction or a publicly announced competition.
(2) (Repealed.)
(3) Land that is private municipal property is sold to the owner of a building lawfully built on it by the mayor without an auction or competition, in the procedure of the ordinance under Art. 8(2).
(4) The sale may be made without an auction or competition, in the procedure of the ordinance under Art. 8(2):
1. between the municipality and the state or between municipalities;
2. when the persons to whom the sale may be made are set by law.
(5) A gift of a property that is private municipal property is made after a decision of the municipal council adopted by three quarters of all councillors.
(6) On the basis of the results of the auction or competition, or of the decision of the municipal council, the mayor issues an order and concludes a contract.
Art. 56. (1) Acts of municipal property are drawn up for the municipal properties on forms approved by the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works and the Minister of Justice.

(2) No acts of municipal property are drawn up for temporary structures, streets, squares, municipal roads and other linear objects of technical infrastructure, unless a special law provides otherwise.

Art. 58. (1) The act of municipal property is drawn up in two copies by an official designated by the mayor. It is signed by the official, approved by the mayor and presented for entry under the Cadastre and Property Register Act within 7 days of its approval.

(2) The first copy is kept in the registry office and the second in the municipality. A copy is sent within 7 days of the entry to the geodesy, cartography and cadastre office, to the regional governor and to the persons to whom the property was given.

(3) A file on a form approved by the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works and the Minister of Justice is kept for each municipal property, with a copy of the act and the documents on the creation, change and end of the municipality's ownership, the rights given to third persons and other data set in the ordinance under Art. 63(3).

(4) The act of municipal property for a state property transferred to the municipality free of charge, or acquired by the municipality by purchase from or exchange with the state, is drawn up under paras. 1–3 after the property is struck off the books of state property under the State Property Act. Within 14 days of the decision of the Council of Ministers, or of the signing of the contract, the competent body strikes the property off the books of state property and hands it over to the municipality.

(5) The act of municipal property for a state property that passed to the municipality by law is drawn up under paras. 1–3 after the property is struck off the books of state property under the State Property Act.
